title: Rule-set compatibility assertor for regional/tier fallback semantics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a "compatibility assertor" that validates routing rule sets (DSL/config) for correct region selection, tier routing semantics, and deterministic fallback model-variant chains before they are accepted into the runtime. This ticket is part of the policy engine refactor to make rule validation modular, testable, and migration-safe.

Scope:
- Normalize incoming DSL into a canonical typed-AST and produce a stable, versioned schema representation.
- Static checks: syntax, required fields, field-deprecation warnings, type coercion, prohibited constructs for private tenants.
- Semantic checks: region-to-tier mapping consistency, tier precedence validation, compatibility of model-variant fallback chains (ensures fallback models are compatible by architecture/quantization/sequence-length), circular-fallback detection, and policy scoping (customer, org, global).
- Behavioral assertions: run a deterministic simulator that executes the rule-set against a corpus of synthetic requests (region distributions, model constraints) to detect surprising route flips and regression of latency/cost metrics.
- Migration helpers: automated transforms for deprecated keys and a dry-run mode that produces diffs for maintainers.
- Tooling: CLI validator (lint + assert), server-side pre-commit hook for policy changes in the config repo, and an API endpoint used by Console to surface validation errors to users.

Trade-offs and decisions considered:
- Strong typing vs. flexible user-facing syntax: adopt a permissive surface (aliases & shorthands) but normalize aggressively into typed-AST for validation and runtime determinism.
- Strict vs. advisory failures: validation will block changes that produce hard safety violations (circular fallback, missing region mapping, incompatible model variant mapping) but emit warnings for non-blocking issues (deprecated fields, recommended batching settings).
- Simulation fidelity vs. speed: the simulator will initially use heuristics (request sampling + deterministic resolution) to catch the majority of logic errors; an optional slower, high-fidelity path will be available for staging.

Acceptance criteria:
- New CLI validator validates and rejects rule-sets with hard-safety violations with clear error messages (error codes documented).
- Validator exposes a --dry-run that outputs normalized AST + suggested migration diffs.
- Integration tests cover region selection permutations, tier precedence edge cases, and fallback chains with at least 95% deterministic coverage.
- Pulled into CI: PRs that modify routing configs must run validator; misrouted test cases should break the PR.
- Console surfaces validation failures with links to the failing rule and a suggested remediation.

Artifacts & references:
- Design note (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/SmartRoutingRefactor
- Draft PR with canonicalizer prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/policy-engine/pull/842
- Routing simulation harness (internal): https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-sim

Rollout plan:
1) Merge validator library behind feature flag and wire into config CI (risk: false positives)
2) Run validator in dry-run mode for one-week snapshot of production configs, iterate on messages
3) Enable blocking mode for new PRs only (old rules grandfathered with warnings)
4) After 2 weeks, enable blocking mode for all config pushes with an emergency bypass for ops
5) Monitor metrics (config rejections, deploy time, misroutes post-deploy) and adjust rules

Metrics to track:
- Number of configs rejected by validator per-sprint
- Number of simulated misroutes detected vs. post-deploy incidents
- Time-to-fix for rejected configs

Longer-term: integrate with console rollouts to do canary validation of policy changes against live traffic and surface drift between simulated and real routing outcomes.
